summary: Charles Schoebel worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin and under Eugène Burnouf, and in 1845 taught German at the Lycée de Reims and the Collège Sainte-Barbe.

Charles Swynnerton was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at University College London and earned an M.A. from the University of Oxford, later serving as headmaster at Ramsey Grammar School.

Charles Taliaferro is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Goddard College, the University of Rhode Island, Brown University, and Harvard Divinity School, and became a professor at St. Olaf College around 1985.

Charles Taylor works in philosophy. He studied at Selwyn House School, McGill University (~1948–1952), and Balliol College, Oxford (~1952–1961), later holding posts at McGill (~1961–1998), Université de Montréal (~1967–1971), and Northwestern University (~2002).

Charles Ulysse Renel worked in Indology and religious studies, completing a Ph.D. under Paul Regnaud at the University of Lyon in 1896. He held posts at Caen Normandy (1897), Franche-Comté (1898), and Lyon (1900).

Charles Wei-hsun Fu worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at National Taiwan University (~1952–1956) and the University of Illinois System (~1965–1969), and held a post at Ohio University (~1969–1973).

Charles Wilkins was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kālinātha. He founded the Asiatic Society in 1784 and served as librarian for the East India Company, the India Office Records, and the India Office Library.
Charles Willemen specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied under William Reynolds Beal Acker and earned a Ph.D. from Ghent University, where he also served as a professor until 2007.

Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, sinology, and Indology. After earning a law doctorate from the University of Liège, he directed Collège Saint-Quirin and became a professor at KU Leuven/Louvain.

Charlotte Krause was an Indologist who studied at Berlin, Marburg, Tübingen, and Leipzig (Ph.D. and Habilitation), as well as under Vijaya Indra Suri. She served as an assistant at Leipzig and later as curator at the Scindia Oriental Institute.
Charlotte Melina Viall studied at the Cornell University College of Agriculture and Life Sciences and at the University of Chicago between approximately 1914 and 1917.

Charlotte Vaudeville specialized in Indology and religious studies. She earned her degrees at the Sorbonne, studied under scholars including Pierre Meile and Louis Renou, and held appointments at the CNRS, EFEO, EPHE, and the Sorbonne.

Chatral Sangye Dorje was a master in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Sera Khandro, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, whom he succeeded alongside Dudjom Rinpoche.

Chatsumarn Kabilsingh works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religion. She studied at Visva-Bharati, McMaster, and Magadh universities, held a post in philosophy and religion at Thammasat University (~1973–2000), and founded Sakyadhita and Yasodhara.

Chen-kuo Lin is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Temple University. He held positions at National Chengchi University, the International Institute for Asian Studies, and served as European Chair of Chinese Studies at Leiden University.
Cheng Huang has held posts at the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, UT Southwestern Medical Center, and Southern Methodist University.
Cheng Yen is a religious studies and Buddhist studies figure who became a disciple of Yinshun in 1963. She founded the Tzu Chi Foundation in 1966 and Tzu Chi University in 2000.
Cheryl A. Crowley is a Japanology scholar who studied under Linda H. Chance, William R. LaFleur, Philip Boas Yampolsky, and Ryuichi Abe.

Chhabilal Neupane works in Indology and philosophy. He earned an M.A. from Indira Gandhi National Open University (2023–2024), taught Sanskrit at Union Academy Senior Secondary School (2019–2023), and held a Darshan post at Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (2023).

Chheangkhy Hok works in linguistics and Indology, and has held posts at the University of Heng Samrin Thbongkhmum in the Department of Khmer Literature and at the Indian Institute of Technology (BHU) Varanasi.
